record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Matrix Theory Arising in Linear Systems and Control
record.context_brief: inducedness of the Frobenius matrix norm
record.original_question: Is the Frobenius norm on the space of m x n real matrices an induced matrix norm if one is allowed to place different norms on the domain R^n and codomain R^m? The source explains that it is not induced when the same norm is used on both spaces, but leaves open whether asymmetric choices of vector norms could induce the Frobenius norm.

evidence.quote: From (4.7) the answer to this question would appear to be related to the following question: Is the Frobenius matrix norm induced?

Since ||I_n||_F = sqrt(n), the answer is no if the domain and range spaces of I_n are assigned the same norms. However, this does not rule out the possibility of assigning different norms to, say R^m and R^n for inducing the Frobenius norm of M in R^{m x n}. This remains a fundamental open problem.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For positive integers $m,n$, the Frobenius norm of a real matrix $A=(a_{ij})\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$ is
$$\|A\|_F=\Bigl(\sum_{i=1}^{m}\sum_{j=1}^{n}a_{ij}^{2}\Bigr)^{1/2}.$$
Given any vector norm $\alpha$ on $\mathbb{R}^{n}$ and any vector norm $\beta$ on $\mathbb{R}^{m}$, the induced (operator) norm of $A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$ is
$$\|A\|_{\alpha,\beta}=\sup_{x\in\mathbb{R}^{n}\setminus\{0\}}\frac{\beta(Ax)}{\alpha(x)}.$$
A matrix norm $\|\cdot\|$ on $\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$ is called induced if there exist a vector norm $\alpha$ on $\mathbb{R}^{n}$ and a vector norm $\beta$ on $\mathbb{R}^{m}$ such that $\|A\|=\|A\|_{\alpha,\beta}$ for every $A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$.

Decide, for $m,n\ge 2$, whether the Frobenius norm $\|\cdot\|_F$ on $\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$ is induced. Equivalently, do there exist vector norms $\alpha$ on $\mathbb{R}^{n}$ and $\beta$ on $\mathbb{R}^{m}$ (possibly different, and not required to be unitarily invariant) such that $\|A\|_F=\|A\|_{\alpha,\beta}$ for all $A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$?
artifact.status_search_result: A subsequent IEEE Transactions on Automatic Control note titled "Is the Frobenius matrix norm induced?" addresses this question and concludes, via a dual-norm argument, that the Frobenius norm is not induced by any pair of vector norms on the domain and codomain (for matrix dimension at least 2); more generally, up to scalar multiple, the spectral norm is the only unitarily invariant induced norm, and the Frobenius case follows.

status_evidence.title: Is the Frobenius matrix norm induced?
status_evidence.snippet: Paper by Haddad and Bernstein in IEEE Transactions on Automatic Control resolving the question.
status_evidence.claim: The Frobenius norm is shown not to be induced by any pair of vector norms on domain and codomain.

status_evidence.title: Is the Frobenius Matrix Norm Induced? (PDF)
status_evidence.snippet: Author-hosted copy of the IEEE TAC note answering the open problem.
status_evidence.claim: Negative resolution: no choice of vector norms on R^n and R^m induces the Frobenius norm.

status_evidence.title: A note on unitarily invariant matrix norms
status_evidence.snippet: The only subordinate unitarily invariant norm is the spectral 2-norm.
status_evidence.claim: As a corollary, the Frobenius norm is not an induced norm.
